top.line: A site factory: a request in a commit makes CI create the repository, the DNS record and the vault.
top.para: Plan on the pull request, apply on merge, seed and verify, an optional Claude Code pass, and a record of it all.

in-short.line: Three things per site, three options, a request folder, plan and apply, credentials, public by default, agents.

question.line: Every site needs a repository, a record and a vault, starting with the Web Summit team site.
question.para: How to go from a commit to a live link.

options.line: By hand, scripts or a CLI, or a CI pipeline.
options.para: Only the pipeline needs no person with the keys.

request.line: A folder per request: site.json, brief.md, and status.json written back by CI.
request.para: Every site has its own history.

pipeline.line: Plan on the pull request; on merge, six steps from repository to record.

credentials.line: A GitHub App, AWS through OpenID Connect, secrets only for sgit and Claude.
credentials.para: No long-lived AWS keys at all.

policy.line: The pipeline has its own policy: one org, two zones, labels by pattern, a daily limit.
policy.para: It can create; only teardown removes.

public.line: The factory and its record are public; only the credentials are not.
public.para: The plan step runs with no secrets; apply only after a merge to main.

agents.line: An agent creates a site by opening a pull request on the control repository.

limits.line: A hypothesis; sgit's token model; an optional, costed Claude pass.

sources.line: My own thinking and earlier articles.
sources.para: With links to the hub and atomic cells.
